summary: How American industrialists in the National Association of Manufacturers, led by J. Howard Pew and Jasper Crane, funded preacher James Fifield's Spiritual Mobilization from the 1930s to the 1950s to fuse Christianity with free-market capitalism against the New Deal.
keywords: First Congregational Church of Los Angeles

evidence.note: Depression and New Deal set off the businessmen's campaign; story proper begins here
Fifield addresses the 1940 NAM convention and becomes the industrialists' inside man
Fifield founds Spiritual Mobilization to rally ministers against the welfare state
NAM's late-1940s PR blitz: ads, school speakers, canned newspaper editorials
Pew and DuPont's Crane lead the NAM faction that bankrolls Fifield
1950 midterm gains credited by backers to Spiritual Mobilization's work
1951 Freedom Under God Fourth of July campaign with Hoover, MacArthur and Hollywood stars
Prayer Breakfast, under God in the Pledge and In God We Trust motto follow, 1953-1956
Fifield quits Spiritual Mobilization in 1957; Pew and Crane switch to Billy Graham
Pew-funded 1958 survey of Christianity Today readers is the latest dated event
Legacy traced to Skousen pocket constitutions and the 2016 Malheur occupation

notes: Primary is the ideology/campaign rather than Fifield, since the story centres on the business-clergy alliance and covers only Fifield's 1935-1957 career, so roles stay empty. The opening on Gilded Age labor and 1890-1930 Christian socialists is treated as background, not covered years. Jasper Crane and Billy Graham left as keywords because of the five-subject cap.
